summary: PROVED source check: Gupta–Murty (1984), Theorem and Lemmas 1–4, give ≥δX/log²X primes for one of 13 candidates, using the O(Y^(4/3)) small-subgroup bound and the survivor inequality 7>2·3. The ES union is W_J(p)=Σ_(a,C)∈J 1[p≡−a mod(4aC−1)], with #hits≥(ΣW_J)²/ΣW_J², but their subgroup argument supplies neither these moments nor fixed-p positivity. FIXED_MODULUS_SHOTS.md §3.3 already performs the decisive transplant: ‘In ES the set at r is A_r, of r-density ≤ τ₃(k)/r = r^{−1+o(1)}’; §6.1 bounds the available certifying moduli by O(p²). Thus the required bounded exponent-box membership and finite search range are not the primitive-root hypotheses.
not_done: No new fixed-p joint-moment bound or impossibility theorem for all Artin-inspired methods is proved.
next: Any new transfer must force membership in the finite divisor box, not merely generation of its ambient subgroup.

summary: PROVED source check: Pintz–Ruzsa II (2020), Theorem 1 and Lemma 6, give K=8 unconditionally and |Σ_(j≤L)e(2^jα)|<0.789401L outside measure ≪N^(−3/5)L^(−100); part I (2003) supplies the lemma and K=7 on GRH. For an ES line with fixed a,b and H consecutive C-values, its exact Fourier sum has modulus H at α=k/(4ab) and ≥0.99H on a union of measure ≥1/(100H). Hence the proposed uniform lacunary large-value estimate fails on the short lines H=polylog N present in the ES range; long-line geometric-sum decay alone supplies no minor-arc error below the expected log²p count. No ES exceptional-set exponent follows (memo §Z2082).
not_done: No new aggregate ES major/minor-arc decomposition; the exact single-line obstruction does not rule out a suitably organized family sum.
next: A usable transfer needs a summed one-sided minor-arc estimate at the log²p scale, not the powers-of-two lemma alone.

summary: PROVED source check: Montgomery–Vaughan (1975), Theorem 1 and §§2–3, give E_G(X)<X^(1−δ), using prime-pair major/minor arcs and zero-density input, not an ES theorem. The exact internal ES sieve cost is supply μ≈t³ and expansion order r≈μ with coefficient/interval error exp(O(t⁴)), t=log X; balancing t⁴≈log N yields the repo's unrefereed 3/4 exponent, whereas μ≈t² gives Vaughan's published 2/3. An ES decomposition R=M+r with M≥c log²N would need Σ|r|²≪N log⁴N exp(−c'(log N)^θ) to yield exponent θ; the Goldbach theorem supplies no such restricted-divisor residual bound. The concrete missing input is the growing-order joint-class or alternative residual estimate, not a small improvement of sieve level (memo §Z2303).
not_done: No ES L²-small residual representation or power-saving exceptional-set theorem is established; the internal 3/4 proof is not independently re-audited in full.
next: Seek an arithmetic residual estimate beyond the growing-order CRT error rather than importing Goldbach's exponent.

summary: PROVED source check: Elsholtz–Technau–Technau (arXiv:1709.04799), abstract/§1.1, explicitly state Wigert's max log τ(n)=(log 2+o(1))log x/log log x. Consequently D_C(p)≤τ(4Cp+1), and for C≤p^A this gives exp(((A+1)log 2+o(1))log p/log log p), an upper bound with no lower-tail content. BM_CORRECTED_COUNT.md §3.1, Proposition 3.1 already constructs primes with ≥2^(k−1) certificates using p≡−1 mod the product of k primes ≡3 mod4 and Linnik's theorem, hence super-polylogarithmic spikes infinitely often. Its decisive conclusion is ‘every two-sided hypothesis |R−M|≤E with E=(log p)^O(1) … is false infinitely often’, which completes the requested fluctuation check.
not_done: The original item has no identifiable Linnik representation-function title; original Wigert/Linnik papers were not accessed, and no such unspecified paper is claimed verified.
next: Retain only one-sided lower-tail hypotheses; maximal-order theorems cannot prove witness positivity.

summary: PROVED source check: Green–Sawhney arXiv:2410.04189v3, Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 4.3, count prime norm values averaged over two coordinates and derive Type II cancellation from product-coordinate Gowers uniformity at L≤X^(3/8), with an extension to X^(1/2−κ). For ES p²+4dc², setting n=4d fixes the field but fixing the coordinate x=p loses that two-coordinate average, and the divisor condition g≡−p mod4cd is not the source's product-form weight. A width-1/N smooth row cutoff grows third derivatives like N³, destroying the published error; varying d also lacks uniform fixed-field constants. More concretely, at p≡1 mod4 a prime value p²+4dc² has no divisor ≡−p mod4cd at all, so the very prime-value event counted is not a Type I certificate (memo §Z2389).
not_done: No fixed-p divisor-weight Gowers or Type II estimate; the retrieved source is v3 (2026), of the paper first submitted in 2024.
next: Formulate and prove a fixed-coordinate residue-restricted divisor estimate before invoking the prime-norm sieve.

summary: PROVED source check: FKM Theorem 1.5 requires bounded-conductor nonexceptional isotypic trace weights and gives error X(1+q/X)^(1/12)q^(−η/2), η<1/24, not cancellation for arbitrary residue indicators. For FIXED_MODULUS_SHOTS.md §3, the local failure indicator is F_q=1−Σ_(r∈A_q)δ_r with |A_q|=q^o(1); its prime sum to q is ≥π(q)−|A_q|−1≈q/log q, contradicting the advertised nonexceptional bounded-conductor bound O(q^(47/48+ε)). CERTIFIED quotient-box/direct-cube checks give |A_942479|=1977 and |A_999983|=127, with local failure densities 0.9979023383 and 0.9998729977; these are point-support sizes, not minimum-conductor measurements. Constants and the additive-character expansion of delta masses are excluded by FKM, full shot failure is not q-periodic, and fixed-q prime densities follow instead from ordinary PNT in progressions (memo §Z2399).
not_done: No universal lower bound for minimal conductor of every centered-indicator representation; no centered admissible trace construction or joint-modulus prime-density estimate is supplied.
next: Separate the constant component and sparse AP atoms explicitly; FKM alone cannot detect the q^o(1)-sized success set.

summary: PROVED source check: Ford–Maynard arXiv:2407.14368, (I)/(II) and Theorems 2.1–2.2, optimize prime detection Σ_(ℓ prime)a_ℓ under prescribed Type I/II data, including prime-free sequences for insufficient Type II width. Divisor conditions are allowed as weights: a_d=Σ_(C≤B)1[d|4Cp+1]1[d≡−1 mod4C] is nonnegative, but the theorem requires new fixed-p distribution estimates and would detect only prime divisors. At p=103,C=2, 825=3·5²·11 has a valid composite divisor 15≡7 mod8 and cofactor 55≡7 mod8, yielding (a,b,C)=(2,7,2), but no prime factor in that class. Thus this framework neither directly counts all divisor-class witnesses nor proves an ES parity barrier or improved exceptional exponent (memo §Z2403).
not_done: No comparison sequence or Type I/II estimates for the fixed-p certificate-divisor weights; no optimal-information theorem for a general divisor-class detector.
next: Any prime-divisor specialization must verify the exact input estimates and acknowledge its stronger target.

summary: PROVED identity: E_J(N)=Σ_(n≤N)Π_(j∈J)(1−I_j(n)) for a finite certificate menu, and the same product over all bounded sorted denominator triples gives literal E_ES(N); using only ★ gives an upper bound, not equality. Harel–Mousset–Samotij Theorem 3.1 (arXiv:1904.08212) assumes a bounded-degree nonnegative polynomial of independent Bernoulli coordinates and entropically stable cores. Success-coordinate expansion has alternating signs; failure coordinates remove signs but have growing degree and correlated arithmetic laws, while E(N) itself is deterministic. Product moments require simultaneous-congruence counts N/lcm+O(1) at growing order, the unproved transfer that cannot be replaced by Bernoulli independence, so no exponent beyond Vaughan's 2/3 or the repo's internal 3/4 follows (memo §Z2408).
not_done: No arithmetic entropic-stability or high-moment estimate; the paper's general-measure preliminary definitions are not mistaken for its independent-Bernoulli sharp theorem.
next: Prove actual growing-order arithmetic correlations rather than assigning independent probabilities to failure coordinates.

summary: PROVED source correction: Ustinov (2008/2009), Theorem 2, counts the SUM of regular-CF Gauss–Kuzmin statistics at fixed denominator b with error b^(5/6)log^(7/6+ε)b, not the number of fractions of length 3. ES₅ uses negative Hirzebruch–Jung length plus a nonresidue condition (DEDEKIND_ES.md §§1,4.6), so specializing b=p does not give the requested sparse event, and even the later Bykovskii–Frolenkov error p^(23/29+ε) exceeds log²p. CERTIFIED direct continuant enumeration, cross-checked on all 76,115 reduced fractions with b≤500, gives totals 2,766,831 regular length-3 versus 1,929,022 HJ length-3 fractions over all 19,552 primes p≡1 mod8 to 10⁶, of which 1,350,392 HJ fractions are nonresidues. At b=17 the counts are 7 versus 2, and at b=49 they are 12 versus 6 with zero nonresidues: this corrects the proposed literature-to-ES statistic rather than extending the repo's existing ES₅ census (memo §Z2412).
evidence: DEDEKIND_ES.md Lemma 1.1, R276 correction in §2, Thm 4.5/Cor 4.6
not_done: No Ustinov exact-length-three theorem was found or assumed; direct enumeration is an explicit substitute, and no twisted short-HJ-cylinder asymptotic at fixed p is proved.
next: The needed input is a nonresidue-twisted short negative-CF count with error o(log²p), not a mean regular-CF length estimate.
